updates.text: Added FlutterFlow, an AI agent that builds native mobile apps from a description
New: 14 use cases showing which agents to use for which job
Added Samepage Bets, feedback to shipped work with PM agents
Added Figma agent, the on-canvas design agent in Figma
Added Wonder, a design canvas that works with coding agents
New workflow: library-true screen to shipped code
Windsurf is now listed as Devin Desktop
Added 5 workflows that chain these tools

agents.name: FlutterFlow
agents.oneLiner: Describe a phone app and its agent builds a native iOS and Android version, backend included.
agents.forWho: Designers and PMs who want a real mobile app without coding
agents.standout: Goes from a plain-language description to an app ready to submit to the App Store and Google Play.
agents.pricing: Free plan; paid from $29/mo billed yearly

agents.name: Samepage Bets
agents.oneLiner: Pulls customer feedback into one place, ranks it, then has agents research, spec and ship the work.
agents.standout: Turns scattered feedback from calls, tickets and chat into scored bets, with a human approving each agent step.
agents.pricing: Free plan; Pro $15/mo, Teams $25/user/mo billed yearly

agents.name: Figma agent
agents.oneLiner: An AI agent inside Figma Design that plans and carries out multi-step design tasks on your canvas.
agents.forWho: Product designers and design teams on paid Figma plans
agents.standout: Builds and refines screens from your own library components, tokens and variables instead of placeholder UI.

agents.name: Wonder
agents.oneLiner: A design canvas where you and your coding agents work on the real product, and the design stays as code.
agents.standout: Runs Claude Code or Codex on your own subscription, each in its own git worktree, beside the design.

agents.name: Figma Make
agents.oneLiner: Turns prompts, frames and design kits into working, editable prototypes inside Figma.
agents.standout: Click any element in the live preview to restyle or re-prompt it, then copy it to canvas.

agents.name: Stitch
agents.oneLiner: Generates mobile and web UI screens plus front-end code from text or sketches.
agents.forWho: Designers and developers exploring early UI
agents.standout: Upload a whiteboard sketch or screenshot and get a digital design you can paste into Figma.

agents.name: Uizard
agents.oneLiner: AI UI design tool that generates screens, themes and prototypes from prompts.
agents.standout: Scan a hand-drawn wireframe or app screenshot and turn it into an editable mockup.

agents.name: Lovable
agents.oneLiner: Builds and hosts full apps from plain-language chat, backend included.
agents.forWho: Non-developers building products and internal tools
agents.standout: Go from a described idea to a deployed app with hosting, auth and payments handled.
agents.pricing: Free plan (daily build credits); paid plans, see site

agents.name: Bolt
agents.oneLiner: Chat-based builder for websites, apps, slides and prototypes with built-in hosting.
agents.standout: Start a build from an existing Figma design or GitHub repo and keep your design system.

agents.name: v0
agents.oneLiner: Prompt-to-web-app builder that plans, codes and deploys full-stack sites.
agents.forWho: Designers and developers shipping web apps
agents.standout: Tweak generated UI visually in Design Mode, sync to GitHub, deploy to Vercel in one click.

agents.name: Replit Agent
agents.oneLiner: Chat agent that writes, tests, fixes and publishes apps for you.
agents.forWho: Founders, PMs and designers without coding skills
agents.standout: Tests the app in a browser while it builds, reports bugs and fixes them itself.
agents.pricing: Free to start; Core from $20/mo ($18 billed annually)

agents.name: Magic Patterns
agents.oneLiner: AI design workspace that turns prompts and PRDs into high-fidelity UI.
agents.standout: Import your component library so generated concepts match your design system, then hand off to a coding agent.

agents.name: Dovetail
agents.oneLiner: Pulls customer feedback from many sources into cited insights, chat and agents.
agents.forWho: Researchers, designers and PMs at larger orgs
agents.standout: Agents automate recurring stakeholder updates and route ranked customer needs to Jira, Linear or Cursor.
agents.pricing: Paid; from $4,800/yr plus credits; 30-day free trial

agents.name: Maze
agents.oneLiner: Recruit participants, run tests and interviews, and get AI-assisted analysis.
agents.standout: Run unmoderated prototype tests with a 6M+ participant panel and auto-generated reports.

agents.name: Listen Labs
agents.oneLiner: AI-moderated customer interviews at scale, from study design to slides.
agents.forWho: UX researchers, PMs and insights teams
agents.standout: An AI moderator interviews participants in 120+ languages and every finding links back to its interview.

agents.name: Outset
agents.oneLiner: Runs hundreds of AI-moderated video, voice or text interviews at once.
agents.standout: Generates the interview guide from your goals, then delivers themes, highlight reels and decks.

agents.name: ChatPRD
agents.oneLiner: AI product-management assistant that drafts, reviews and prototypes specs.
agents.standout: Turns meeting notes into a PRD, scores it, then opens it in v0, Lovable or Cursor.

agents.name: Linear Agent
agents.oneLiner: Issue tracker where AI agents are workspace members you can assign work to.
agents.standout: Delegate an issue to Cursor, Codex or ChatPRD and watch each change and its reasoning.
agents.pricing: Free plan includes agents; paid from $10/user/mo billed yearly

agents.name: Notion Agent
agents.oneLiner: Workspace agent that builds and edits pages and databases across connected apps.
agents.forWho: PMs and teams documenting work in Notion
agents.standout: Custom Agents run on a schedule to answer Slack questions, route tasks and post updates.
agents.pricing: Trial on Free; full agent on Business, $20/seat/mo

agents.name: Rovo
agents.oneLiner: Search, chat and agents across Jira, Confluence and connected tools.
agents.standout: Agents use links between people, projects and code to draft roadmaps and route backlog work.
agents.pricing: Included with Atlassian Cloud Standard, Premium or Enterprise (usage credits)

agents.name: Claude Code
agents.oneLiner: Agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files and runs commands.
agents.standout: Kick off a task from Slack or GitHub and get back a pull request.
agents.pricing: Included with paid Claude plans; Team $20/seat/mo billed annually

agents.name: Cursor
agents.oneLiner: AI code editor whose agents plan, build and test features.
agents.standout: Launch cloud agents in parallel that build, test and demo features on their own machines.
agents.pricing: Free plan; paid plans on site

agents.name: GitHub Copilot
agents.oneLiner: Coding agent that picks up GitHub issues and returns reviewed pull requests.
agents.standout: Hand an issue to the cloud agent and get a pull request back for review.

agents.name: Codex
agents.oneLiner: Coding agent running in the cloud, desktop app, IDE and terminal.
agents.standout: Runs tasks in the cloud while your laptop is closed and checks work with browser tools.
agents.pricing: Included with ChatGPT Plus, Pro and Business

agents.name: Devin Desktop
agents.oneLiner: AI IDE, formerly Windsurf, with a command center for many agents.
agents.standout: A lead agent splits long tasks among subagents that each open their own pull requests.

agents.name: Claude
agents.oneLiner: General AI assistant on web, desktop and mobile for writing, analysis and research.
agents.forWho: Designers, PMs and anyone doing knowledge work
agents.standout: Paid plans also include Claude Code, so one subscription covers thinking and building.

agents.name: ChatGPT agent
agents.oneLiner: ChatGPT mode that uses its own browser to complete multi-step tasks.
agents.forWho: Anyone delegating web research and busywork
agents.standout: Researches across sites and builds a slideshow or spreadsheet, asking before important steps.
agents.pricing: Included with ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise

agents.name: Comet
agents.oneLiner: AI browser with a built-in assistant that researches and acts on pages.
agents.forWho: People who live in the browser
agents.standout: Compare how different sources cover a topic, or draft an email reply, without leaving the page.

workflows.title: Library-true screen to shipped code
steps: Draft the screen with the Figma agent using your own components
Bring it into Wonder and explore variations on the canvas
Have Claude Code build the chosen version in its own worktree
workflows.outcome: A reviewed preview built from your design system, ready to merge

workflows.title: Idea to tested prototype in a day
steps: Draft the PRD from meeting notes in ChatPRD
Open the spec in v0 to build a clickable app
Run an unmoderated prototype test with Maze participants
workflows.outcome: A working prototype with real user feedback attached

workflows.title: Interviews straight into the roadmap
steps: Run AI-moderated interviews at scale with Listen Labs
Bring transcripts and feedback into Dovetail for cited themes
Route ranked needs to Linear as issues
workflows.outcome: Customer evidence linked to every roadmap issue

workflows.title: Whiteboard sketch to Figma prototype
steps: Photograph the sketch and generate screens in Stitch
Paste the designs into Figma for cleanup
Turn the frames into a working prototype with Figma Make
workflows.outcome: An interactive prototype built from a rough sketch

workflows.title: Hand UI fixes to a coding agent
steps: Log design QA issues in Linear
Delegate each issue to Cursor or Codex from Linear
Review the returned pull requests with GitHub Copilot code review
workflows.outcome: Design polish shipped as reviewed pull requests

workflows.title: Competitive scan to product brief
steps: Have ChatGPT agent browse competitor sites and build a comparison
Summarize gaps and opportunities with Claude
Save the brief and next steps in Notion with Notion Agent
workflows.outcome: A sourced competitor brief your team can act on

usecases.job: Turn a PRD into a clickable prototype
usecases.for: PMs and designers with a spec who need something people can click
usecases.answer: Draft or tighten the PRD in ChatPRD, open it in v0 to build a working web prototype, then put it in front of real users with a Maze test. You end up with a clickable app and real feedback on it, often in a single day.

setup.does: Turns your notes into a PRD and scores it, so weak spots show up before you build. It can open the spec straight in v0.
Builds the clickable web app from the spec. Tweak the UI visually in Design Mode, then deploy in one click and share the link.
Runs an unmoderated test of the prototype with people from its participant panel and writes the report for you.

alternatives.when: The prototype has to look like your real product. Import your component library and it turns the PRD into high-fidelity UI.
You need more than a demo. Hosting, sign-in and payments come built in.
Your team lives in Figma and wants the prototype next to the designs.

usecases.watchOut: Don't polish the prototype before the test. The point is to find out which parts of the spec are wrong while they're still cheap to change.

usecases.job: Generate UI that uses your own design system
usecases.for: Product designers and design system teams tired of generic AI screens
usecases.answer: Start in Figma with the Figma agent, which builds screens from your real library components, tokens and variables. When you want to see it as code, move into Wonder, where the design stays as code and a coding agent builds the version you pick.

setup.does: Drafts and refines screens from your own components, tokens and variables instead of placeholder UI. It comes with paid Figma plans.
Explore variations on a canvas where the design is kept as code, so what you pick is what gets built.
Builds the chosen version. Wonder runs it in its own git worktree, and you get the change back to review.

alternatives.when: You want concepts outside Figma that still match your system. Import your component library, then hand off to a coding agent.
You're starting a build from an existing Figma design or GitHub repo and want to keep your design system.

usecases.watchOut: AI is only as on-brand as your library. If your components and tokens are messy in Figma, the agent will copy the mess faithfully.

usecases.job: Turn a Figma design into production code
usecases.for: Designers and design engineers who want their work shipped as designed
usecases.answer: If the work has to land in your real codebase, give the design to a coding agent that works in that repo. Wonder keeps the design and the code side by side and runs Claude Code for you, and GitHub Copilot reviews the pull request. For a brand new app, Bolt can start a build straight from your Figma file.

setup.does: Keeps the design as code next to the product and runs Claude Code or Codex on your own subscription to build it.
Reads your codebase, edits the files, runs the commands and hands back a pull request.
Reviews the pull request on GitHub before anyone merges it.

alternatives.when: It's a new app, not a change to an existing one. Start the build from the Figma design and keep your design system.
Your engineers already work in Cursor. Its agents build, test and demo the feature.
It's a web app and you want it deployed to Vercel in one click.

usecases.watchOut: Review the pull request the way you'd review a junior designer's mockup. Check spacing, states and edge cases, not just the happy path.

usecases.job: Turn a whiteboard sketch into a prototype
usecases.for: Designers and PMs who think on paper first
usecases.answer: Photograph the sketch and let Stitch turn it into a digital design, paste that into Figma to clean it up, then make it clickable with Figma Make. If you're not a designer, Uizard is the gentler start.

setup.does: Turns a photo of a whiteboard sketch or a screenshot into a digital design you can paste into Figma, plus front-end code.
Turns the cleaned-up frames into a working prototype. Click any element in the preview to restyle or re-prompt it.

alternatives.when: You're a PM or founder without design skills. It scans a hand-drawn wireframe into an editable mockup.
The screens should be built from your team's own Figma library from the start.

usecases.watchOut: Write short labels on the sketch, like search, filters or results. Clear words leave the generator less to guess.

usecases.job: Prototype a new feature inside your real product
usecases.for: Product teams who are done with throwaway prototypes
usecases.answer: Use Wonder. It's a design canvas on your actual product where the design stays as code, and it runs a coding agent like Codex to build what you design. If you just want a quick build from a GitHub repo, Bolt can start from the repo and keep your design system.

setup.does: Design on the real product, with the design kept as code instead of a separate mockup.
Builds the change in the cloud, even with your laptop closed, and checks its work with browser tools.

alternatives.when: You want a quick build that starts from your GitHub repo or Figma file and keeps your design system.
An engineer is pairing with you. Cursor's cloud agents build, test and demo features in parallel.

usecases.watchOut: Prototyping on real code means real constraints show up early. That's the point, so don't fight it.

usecases.for: Researchers, designers and PMs sitting on a pile of transcripts
usecases.answer: Bring the transcripts and the rest of your feedback into Dovetail, which turns them into insights that cite their sources. Then use Claude to shape the themes into a readout people will actually read, and log what matters in Linear.

setup.does: Pulls interviews and feedback from many sources into cited insights you can chat with.
Turns the cited themes into a tight readout or brief for stakeholders.
Logs the needs that matter as issues, so the evidence travels with the work.

alternatives.when: You haven't run the interviews yet. It writes the guide, runs them and delivers themes, highlight reels and decks.
Your interviews happen in many languages. Every finding links back to the interview it came from.

usecases.watchOut: Read the quotes behind a theme before you present it. Citations are there so you can check the summary, so check it.

usecases.job: Run user interviews at scale with an AI moderator
usecases.for: Research teams and PMs who need many conversations, fast
usecases.answer: Outset writes the interview guide from your goals and runs hundreds of AI-moderated interviews at once. Pick Listen Labs instead when you need many languages. Either way, keep the results in Dovetail so themes add up over time.

setup.does: Generates the guide from your research goals, runs video, voice or text interviews in parallel, then delivers themes and highlight reels.
Holds the results next to the rest of your customer feedback, with every insight citing its source.

alternatives.when: You're interviewing in more than one language. Its AI moderator works in 120+ languages and links every finding to its interview.
You need people to use a prototype, not talk about it. Run an unmoderated test instead.

usecases.watchOut: An AI moderator scales your guide. If the guide asks leading questions, you get leading answers at scale, so pilot it on two or three people first.

usecases.job: Test a prototype with real users
usecases.for: Designers and PMs who want evidence before engineering starts
usecases.answer: Build the prototype in Figma Make, then run an unmoderated test in Maze, which recruits people from its own panel and writes the report. You get real reactions without scheduling a single call.

setup.does: Turns your frames into a working prototype people can click through.
Recruits participants from a 6M+ panel, runs the test unmoderated and generates the report.

alternatives.when: The prototype needs to be a deployed web app, not a click-through.
You want conversations, not task completion. It runs AI-moderated interviews at scale.

usecases.watchOut: Write tasks as goals, like find a plan for a team of five, not as instructions like click Pricing. Otherwise you're testing your copy, not your design.

usecases.job: Turn customer feedback into a spec
usecases.for: PMs drowning in calls, tickets and Slack threads
usecases.answer: Samepage Bets pulls feedback from calls, tickets and chat into one place and ranks it into scored bets. Take the winning bet into ChatPRD to write and score the PRD, then hand the work out in Linear.

setup.does: Collects scattered feedback and ranks it into scored bets, then has agents research and spec the work, with you approving each step.
Writes the PRD and scores it, so you know it's ready before engineers see it.
Turns the spec into issues you can delegate to Cursor, Codex or ChatPRD, and shows each change and its reasoning.

alternatives.when: You're at a larger org with a research team. Its agents route ranked customer needs to Jira, Linear or Cursor.
Your team runs on Jira and Confluence. Its agents draft roadmaps and route backlog work.

usecases.watchOut: Ranked feedback tells you what's loud, not what's important. Keep the call on which bet to take with a person.

usecases.job: Write a PRD from meeting notes
usecases.for: Product managers who'd rather decide than format docs
usecases.answer: Use ChatPRD. Paste in your meeting notes and it drafts the PRD, scores it, and can open it in v0, Lovable or Cursor when you're ready to build. Keep the final spec where your team works with Notion Agent.

setup.does: Turns meeting notes into a PRD and scores it, so you see what's weak before the review.
Builds and edits the spec page and its databases in your Notion workspace.

alternatives.when: You want a thinking partner for the hard tradeoffs, not a template.
Your specs live in Confluence and your work lives in Jira.

usecases.watchOut: Treat the score as a checklist, not a verdict. Only you know whether it's the right problem to solve.

usecases.for: PMs and designers prepping a strategy review or a kickoff
usecases.answer: Send ChatGPT agent to browse competitor sites and build the comparison, ask Claude to pull out the gaps and opportunities, and save the brief in Notion with Notion Agent. Check every claim against the sources before you share it.

setup.does: Browses competitor sites in its own browser and builds the comparison as a spreadsheet or slides, asking before important steps.
Reads the comparison and writes up the gaps and opportunities.
Saves the brief and next steps where the team will find them.

alternatives.when: You'd rather browse yourself. Its assistant compares how different sources cover a topic without leaving the page.

usecases.watchOut: Agents read marketing pages, and marketing pages flatter. Pair the scan with real reviews or customer calls before you draw conclusions.

usecases.for: Designers whose polish tickets sit in the backlog forever
usecases.answer: Log each fix in Linear and delegate it straight to a coding agent like Cursor or Codex, then review what comes back with GitHub Copilot code review. Small UI fixes stop waiting for a sprint.

setup.does: Logs each fix and delegates it to Cursor or Codex, showing every change and its reasoning.
Its cloud agents build, test and demo each fix in parallel.
Reviews the pull request before it's merged.

alternatives.when: Your team is on ChatGPT. Codex runs the fixes in the cloud and checks them with browser tools.
You want to kick fixes off from Slack or GitHub and get pull requests back.

usecases.watchOut: Write each issue like a tiny spec: the screen, what's wrong, what right looks like, and a screenshot. Vague tickets get vague fixes.

usecases.job: Build a working app without writing code
usecases.for: PMs, designers and founders who can't code but need a real product
usecases.answer: Lovable is the default. Get the idea down as a spec in ChatPRD, open it in Lovable, and it builds and deploys a full app with hosting, sign-in and payments handled. Pick Replit Agent if you want it to test the app in a browser and fix its own bugs as it goes.

setup.does: Gets the idea down as a spec first, then opens it in Lovable.
Builds and hosts the full app from plain-language chat, backend included.

alternatives.when: You want an agent that tests the app in a browser while it builds and fixes what breaks.
You're starting from an existing Figma design or GitHub repo.
It's a web app and you want to tweak the UI visually before you deploy.
Pick it when the app needs to be a native iPhone and Android app in the stores.

usecases.watchOut: These tools get you to a working app fast. Before real customers use it, have someone technical check security, data and costs.

usecases.job: Automate status updates and stakeholder reports
usecases.for: PMs and leads who spend Friday afternoons writing updates
usecases.answer: Use the agent that lives where your work does. Notion Agent can run on a schedule to post updates and route tasks, and Claude can draft the part that needs judgment. Teams on Jira and Confluence should use Rovo, and research teams can let Dovetail's agents send recurring stakeholder updates.

setup.does: Custom Agents run on a schedule to post updates, answer Slack questions and route tasks.
Drafts the part that needs judgment: what changed, why it matters and what you need from people.

alternatives.when: Your team runs on Jira and Confluence. Its agents work across both.
The updates are about research and customer insight.

usecases.watchOut: Automate the gathering, not the judgment. Read each update before it goes out, at least for the first month.
